name: ch13_auto_scrape_calm
alt: Split picture: two auto drivers shout at each other over a scrape on the left, and on the right one driver checks on the other and both bend over the bumper together.
scene: A split-panel street scene at a busy Chennai traffic signal, divided by a thin vertical line, the same two yellow-and-green auto-rickshaws touching bumper to bumper in both halves with a small grey scratch on one mudguard. LEFT panel: the first driver (about 40, khaki uniform shirt, white veshti folded at the knee, thin moustache) has leapt out with his arm flung up and mouth wide open; the second driver (younger, khaki shirt, towel on shoulder) is already out too, finger pointing, both red-faced; behind them a crowd of onlookers gathers and two motorbikes honk, shown by small jagged sound marks, and nobody is looking at the scratch. A bold label "SHOUT" sits at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same first driver walks over with an open palm and a concerned face, a small speech bubble with a tiny heart icon; then both drivers crouch side by side over the bumper looking at the scratch together, one pointing at it calmly, and a few rupee notes change hands between them with a shrug and a half-smile. The road behind is calm, traffic light green. A bold label "CALM" at the top of the right panel. Hot midday light, bright colours, a lesson in how the first move sets the whole tone.

key: A new principal takes over a school
name: ch13_principal_staffroom_chai
alt: A new school principal sits drinking chai with teachers in the staff room, listening, while protest placards lean unused against the wall.
scene: A warm interior view of an Indian school staff room: long wooden table, steel chairs, a wall clock, a notice board with timetables, a window showing a playground. On the LEFT, against the wall, three cardboard protest placards lean forgotten, their text hidden, one with a drawn thumbs-down. In the CENTRE, the new principal (a woman in her late 40s, cotton sari in teal, spectacles, hair in a bun) sits at the table not at its head but among the teachers, holding a small glass of chai, leaning forward to listen. Around her three teachers: an older man in a half-sleeve shirt with folded arms slowly loosening, a young woman in a salwar kameez showing a phone photo of her child, and a middle-aged man in a sweater vest smiling for the first time. Steam rises from glasses of chai and a plate of biscuits sits in the middle. A small wall calendar shows two weeks crossed off with ticks to show time spent before any meeting. An inset bubble above the principal shows a tiny school building with a heart, her words of gratitude. A bold label "LISTEN FIRST" across the top centre. Soft morning light, a mood of ice slowly melting between people who came ready to fight.

key: A chai-wallah near a Bengaluru tech park
name: ch13_chai_regulars_price
alt: Split picture: regulars happily pay two rupees more at a friendly chai stall, while customers angrily type reviews about a cold chain cafe's price rise.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a roadside chai stall under a tree near tall glass office towers in Bengaluru; the chai-wallah (about 50, checked lungi, sleeveless vest, towel on shoulder, broad smile) pours tea from a height into small glasses. Two young office workers with lanyards stand at the stall chatting with him; one hands over coins without a second look. A small chalk slate on the stall shows the price going up with the text "+2" and a green tick beside it. A little speech bubble from the chai-wallah shows a baby rattle, him asking about the new baby, and a biscuit sits on a saucer. A bold label "FRIEND" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: a cold, glassy chain cafe counter with a printed price board also showing "+2", a bored barista behind the till, and two customers outside on the pavement frowning at their phones, thumbs typing; above the phones float small one-star rating icons and an angry face badge. A bold label "STRANGER" at the top of the right panel. Warm sunny light on the left, cooler bluish light on the right, showing that the same price rise lands very differently through years of goodwill.

key: The residents' association of a Pune housing
name: ch13_society_samosa_protest
alt: Protesting residents at a housing society gate receive tea and samosas and a thank-you note from the secretary instead of a legal notice.
scene: A daytime wide view of the entrance gate of a Pune apartment society: a blue metal gate, a small security cabin, tall buildings behind with balconies and drying clothes, a gulmohar tree dropping leaves. On the LEFT, four residents stand with handmade protest placards (text hidden, only arrows and a rupee-up symbol): a retired man in a white kurta, a woman in a nightie-and-dupatta morning outfit, a young man in a T-shirt, and an aunty with a steel bottle. In the CENTRE, the society secretary (50s, pressed shirt, reading glasses on his head) walks down from the building carrying a big steel tray with glasses of tea and a plate of samosas, smiling. Behind him a crumpled stiff legal notice lies in a dustbin with a red cross badge beside it. On the gate a white paper note is taped up, reading "THANK YOU". On the RIGHT, a small inset bubble shows the next morning: one protester sweeping leaves with a broom and a calendar showing the weekend meeting with two hands shaking. A bold label "HONEY, NOT LAW" across the top. Warm morning light and a relieved, softening mood among the protesters.

key: A senior umpire at a local cricket tournament
name: ch13_umpire_two_explanations
alt: Split picture: one umpire folds his arms and says it was out, while another kneels with a stick diagram showing the captain the angle from square leg.
scene: A split-panel illustration on the edge of a dusty local cricket ground, a thin vertical line down the middle, stumps and a boundary rope visible in both halves. LEFT panel: an umpire (about 55, white coat, wide-brimmed white hat) stands stiffly with arms crossed and chin up, a speech bubble with a big number "20" and a stopped hand icon, saying his twenty years settle it; the young team captain (about 25, coloured jersey, cap backwards) glares with fists clenched, a red cross badge between them. A bold label "CLOSED" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: a second umpire in the same white coat crouches beside the captain and draws a simple diagram in the dust with a stick: the stumps, a dot for square leg, and a dot at the boundary with dashed sightlines showing the tight angle; the captain leans in with hands on his knees, nodding, frown fading; a green tick badge floats above them. A bold label "OPEN" at the top of the right panel. Afternoon sun, long shadows, the contrast between an order and an explanation that respects the listener's point of view.

key: At a crowded Mumbai railway booking counter
name: ch13_railway_counter_kind
alt: At a crowded railway booking counter, a passenger speaks kindly to a tired clerk, who smiles and offers him a better berth.
scene: A close view through the barred window of a railway reservation counter in a busy Mumbai station. Behind the steel grille sits the clerk (about 45, grey uniform shirt, spectacles pushed up, forehead damp), surrounded by piles of forms and a computer screen; small jagged angry speech marks fade on the wall behind him from the morning's shouting. In front of the window, the passenger (about 30, blue formal shirt, backpack, reservation form in hand) leans in with a gentle, sympathetic face, a speech bubble with a small sun-behind-cloud icon showing he noticed the tough day. Behind him a long queue of three or four impatient people with bags. The clerk is mid-sigh turning into a smile, and on his screen an inset shows a train coach diagram with one berth highlighted in green and an upward arrow, a better berth than asked for. The quoted text "TOUGH DAY, SIR" sits in the passenger's speech bubble. A bold label "KIND WORD" at the top of the frame. Fluorescent station light with a warm glow around the counter window, showing a small kindness opening a small favour.

key: Outside a Delhi wedding hall, a neighbour
name: ch13_wedding_gate_neighbour
alt: Outside a wedding hall at night, a bride's uncle agrees with an angry neighbour filming blocked cars, and helpers move the two cars from his gate.
scene: An evening street outside a Delhi wedding hall lit with strings of marigold-coloured fairy lights and a decorated entrance arch on the RIGHT. On the LEFT, a neighbour's house with a green iron gate; two guest cars are parked across it. In front of the gate the neighbour (about 50, cardigan over kurta, slippers) holds up his phone filming, frowning. In the CENTRE, the bride's uncle (about 55, cream sherwani, saffa turban, moustache) faces him with both palms open and a sympathetic nod, a speech bubble reading "YOU ARE RIGHT". Between them, a small inset shows the neighbour's phone with a group chat icon and a send button about to be pressed, fading. Behind them a young cousin in a kurta jogs toward the cars swinging car keys and a driver is already opening one door; a curved arrow shows the cars backing away from the gate. In the neighbour's other hand a dotted motion line shows the phone sliding back into his pocket. A bold label "AGREE FIRST" across the top. Festive night light, though the background stays the light off-white of the house style; mood turning from confrontation to relief.

key: Your new flat's bathroom ceiling leaks
name: ch13_flat_leak_site_office
alt: Split picture: a flat owner storms into a builder's site office waving photos, and in the second panel chats warmly with the engineer before asking for help with the leak.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves inside a small builder's site office in Gurugram with a desk, a blueprint roll, hard hats on a shelf, and a window showing a half-built tower with a crane. A small inset at the top centre shows the problem: a bathroom ceiling with a brown damp patch and drips into a bucket. LEFT panel: the flat owner (about 35, polo shirt, umbrella under arm) bursts in waving a fan of photos, mouth wide, while the site engineer (about 30, reflective vest, hard hat) leans back with folded arms and a closed face; a red cross badge. A bold label "STORM IN" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same owner sits across the desk with a relaxed smile, pointing out of the window at the new tower, a phone showing the leak photo laid on the desk; the engineer leans forward with a notebook writing, and a small calendar beside him shows a visit circled this week, with a green tick. A bold label "ASK FOR HELP" at the top of the right panel. Grey monsoon light outside, warmer inside on the right side, showing how the friendly opening makes the builder want to fix the leak.

key: A toddler at a family function refuses
name: ch13_toddler_phone_tumbler
alt: Split picture: an adult grabs at a phone and the toddler screams and clutches it, while another adult kneels and offers a shiny steel tumbler and the toddler drops the phone.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a family function in an Indian home, divided by a thin vertical line, marigold garlands on the wall behind and a few blurred guests in festive clothes. LEFT panel: a toddler (about 2, small silk kurta, chubby cheeks) sits on a durrie clutching a mobile phone with both fists; an adult uncle (40s, bright shirt) towers over him reaching down to grab it; the toddler is screaming, mouth open, tears flying, with jagged sound marks and a red cross badge. A bold label "GRAB" at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same toddler sits calmly while an aunt (30s, pink salwar kameez) kneels at his eye level with a big smile, holding out a shiny steel tumbler of water with a little sparkle star on its rim; the toddler reaches for the tumbler with both hands and the phone drops to the floor beside him, shown with a small dotted fall line; a green tick floats above. A bold label "OFFER" at the top of the right panel. Warm festive light, a playful mood showing that a friendly offer beats force even with a stubborn little fist.

name: ch13_dosa_owner_counter
alt: A regular diner speaks warmly to a restaurant owner at the counter about a cold dosa, and a hot dosa and a free filter coffee arrive.
scene: An interior view of a busy South Indian restaurant in Hyderabad: steel tables, a menu board with icons of dosa and idli, a cash counter with a small brass bell on the RIGHT. On the LEFT, a family table with a plate holding a limp dosa with a blue snowflake badge showing it is cold, a waiter passing in the background with a tray, not being snapped at. In the CENTRE, the diner (about 40, half-sleeve shirt, glasses) stands at the counter with a friendly open-hand gesture, talking to the owner (60s, white shirt, sandalwood mark on forehead, reading glasses on a cord) who listens with concern and nods. A speech bubble above the diner shows a calendar with Sunday circled and a small heart, standing for every Sunday visit. On the RIGHT, the result: a waiter arrives carrying a crisp golden dosa with steam curls and a steel tumbler-and-davara of filter coffee, a small "FREE" tag on the coffee. A bold label "PRAISE, THEN THE PROBLEM" across the top. Warm restaurant light, a feeling that respect for the owner turned a complaint into a better service.

key: In many Indian homes, a guest is offered
name: ch13_guest_water_tea
alt: In an Indian living room, a host offers a glass of water and tea to two guests who have come to settle a quarrel before anyone talks.
scene: A warm interior view of a middle-class Indian living room: a sofa with a crocheted cover, a low wooden centre table, a wall calendar and framed family photo. On the LEFT, two guests sit on the sofa, a man in his 50s in a formal shirt with a stiff face and a woman in a cotton sari holding a folder of papers on her lap, plainly here to settle a dispute; a small storm-cloud badge floats above the folder. In the CENTRE, the host (about 55, kurta and pyjama, warm smile) bends forward offering a steel tray with two glasses of water first, and his wife (sari, bindi) follows from the kitchen doorway on the RIGHT with cups of tea and a plate of biscuits, steam curling. A dotted numbered path along the bottom shows the order: a water glass marked "1", a tea cup marked "2", and the folder marked "3" last. Above the guests the storm cloud is already shrinking. A bold label "TEA FIRST" across the top centre. Soft afternoon light through a window with a curtain, a gentle mood of a ritual that starts every hard talk with something warm.
